summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and portal hypertension, was admitted with worsening dyspnea and cough due to a recurrent right pleural effusion. He developed spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, requiring antibiotic treatment, and suffered a variceal bleed that was not amenable to endoscopic banding. He underwent an emergent TIPS procedure, which successfully reduced portal pressure and stopped the bleeding. He received 7 units of packed red blood cells and was managed for hepatic encephalopathy and hyponatremia. A new 2.0 cm liver lesion meeting OPTN 5b criteria was identified on MRI, and cardiac catheterization revealed patent bypass grafts with native coronary disease. The TIPS improved his hydrothorax and ascites, and he was discharged home on medications including ciprofloxacin, lactulose, rifaximin, and reduced-dose warfarin, with plans for transplant evaluation and close follow-up.
problems: Malignant neoplasm of liver, primary, unspecified as to type
